response.sql: WITH state_totals AS (SELECT c.state_county_province AS state, COALESCE(SUM(ft.transaction_amount), 0) AS total FROM Financial_Transactions ft JOIN Accounts a ON a.account_id = ft.account_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id GROUP BY c.state_county_province), shares AS (SELECT state, total, total * 1.0 / SUM(total) OVER () AS share FROM state_totals), with_avg AS (SELECT state, total, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT SUM(total) AS combined_total, AVG(share) AS avg_share_of_above_avg_states, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM with_avg WHERE share > avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: Customers with a NULL state_county_province form one group (via GROUP BY on NULL); empty-string states are treated as their own distinct state value, not merged with NULL.
A state whose transactions all have NULL amounts still counts as a state with total 0 (it is included in the average share across states).
The sum of all state totals is nonzero, so shares are well defined.
